items.title: 67426_Hayes Pillars oral history interview
items.q: we sent to Utica, New York, and got a fella named Goodson.

ctx.x: That was the style of the cabarets back in that day. We found out that by working all night and sometimes early and late in the morning a -- that our salary would run for a week around about $20-$25, and sometimes $30.00 a week. Which wasn't too bad during that time, in the Depression. We worked there with Chester Clark's band all through the following year through the Christmas holidays. And we gave him our notice because we were offered a job -- Jeter and myself, decided to organize a band of our own and we was…

In the band we had A. G. Godley, the drummer; we Had Harry Sweets Edison, we had -- our reed section and we sent to Utica, New York, and got a fella named Goodson. His nickname was Serp, on the piano. And we -- on the bass we had an old gentleman, much older than us, that we had known back in the Alphonso Trent days, his days was [Nunu], I can't think of his
last name now, can you think of his last name? Can you think of his last name, Charles? Well anyway, we opened. And the band was a riot --
